title: Knowledge check: Anatomy of an Express Application

questions.prompt: In Anatomy of an Express Application, which statement best describes Importing Express?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Anatomy of an Express Application: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Trace the request from client through middleware and route/service logic to its response. Keep HTTP concerns separate from business rules and data access.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Connect this syllabus point to Anatomy of an Express Application: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
questions.explanation: Connect this syllabus point to Anatomy of an Express Application: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Anatomy of an Express Application?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Express turns HTTP requests into handler calls, but the application still needs to use correct methods, status codes, headers, environment configuration, and a predictable server lifecycle.
questions.answer_key: Express turns HTTP requests into handler calls, but the application still needs to use correct methods, status codes, headers, environment configuration, and a predictable server lifecycle.
questions.explanation: Express turns HTTP requests into handler calls, but the application still needs to use correct methods, status codes, headers, environment configuration, and a predictable server lifecycle.

questions.prompt: A change related to Anatomy of an Express Application appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
